analysis_summary: Solution Pro proposes a fractal three-layer Loop architecture (Project/Domain/Phase) with Python deterministic skeleton and LLM semantic decision hybrid. The system decomposes into 7 logically independent Worker units aligned with architectural layers: foundation infrastructure, loop engine, quality gate, safety/resilience, dream loop, meta-loop, and observability/security. Dependency graph is a clean DAG with CoreInfrastructure as the root.

workers.task_description: Build the Python deterministic skeleton framework serving as the system backbone. Implement Blackboard Manager with JSON unified serialization (D2), atomic rename for crash-safe writes, and per-stage locking for concurrent access control. This Worker establishes the shared state mechanism that all other components depend upon. Deliverables include: (1) Blackboard Manager class with JSON read/write/atomic-rename, (2) per-stage lock manager with unique task ID enforcement, (3) Python skeleton framework with entry points for Loop engine integration, (4) SHA-256 integrity verification for state files, (5) unit tests for atomic write, lock contention, and crash recovery scenarios.

workers.task_description: Implement the fractal three-layer Loop engine with nested execution and interrupt propagation. Layer 1: Project Loop (outer loop, strategic planning, timeout 8h+). Layer 2: Domain Loop (middle loop, tactical coordination, timeout 2h). Layer 3: Phase Loop (inner loop, execution optimization, timeout 30min). Implement interrupt propagation mechanism where outer loop interrupts cascade to inner loops. Implement DAG scheduling engine with simple priority queue (D4), topological sort for dependency resolution, and max 6 concurrent task execution. Deliverables include: (1) FractalLoopEngine class with three-layer nesting and timeout enforcement, (2) InterruptPropagator for cascade termination with state preservation, (3) DAGScheduler with priority queue + topological sort, (4) concurrency limiter (max 6 parallel tasks), (5) deadlock detection → re-planning trigger, (6) integration tests for nested loop execution, interrupt cascading, and DAG parallel scheduling.

workers.task_description: Implement the three-layer Quality Gate for output validation at every stage transition. Layer 1: Pydantic deterministic validation (field existence, type checking, acyclic dependencies) as fast filter. Layer 2: LLM-as-Judge semantic evaluation using same-model-family with strict isolation (D10) — evaluates architectural soundness, principle alignment, quality, and feasibility with independent perspective from Executor. Layer 3: Combined decision merging L1+L2 results into PASS / CONDITIONAL / FAIL. Implement UTD (Update-Then-Downgrade) strategy with max 3 rejection rounds and circuit breaker for high reject rate mitigation (R1, RTO 4.5min). Deliverables include: (1) QualityGate class with three-layer pipeline, (2) PydanticValidator (Layer 1), (3) LLMJudge with strict isolation and independent prompt (Layer 2), (4) DecisionMerger (Layer 3), (5) circuit breaker with UTD strategy and max 3 rounds, (6) unit tests for each layer and integration tests for combined flow.

workers.task_description: Implement three safety and resilience subsystems. (1) Dead-loop circuit breaker: three-level detection (iteration count threshold, token consumption anomaly, output semantic similarity), three-level progressive response (warning → throttle → halt), circuit breaker state machine (closed → open → half-open). (2) Fault recovery: four-stage decision tree (detect → diagnose → recover → verify), fast path for known failure patterns, cross-vendor fallback for cloud API unavailability (R3, RTO 2.5min). (3) Direction deviation detection: three-layer hybrid approach combining Embedding similarity scoring, Goal Tree structural comparison, and IDS (Isolation Distribution Shift) for semantic drift detection. Implement native Structured Output (D3) as the LLM output validation mechanism replacing xgrammar. Deliverables include: (1) DeadLoopDetector with three-level detection, (2) CircuitBreaker state machine, (3) FaultRecoveryEngine with four-stage decision tree + cross-vendor fallback, (4) DirectionDeviationDetector with hybrid three-layer approach, (5) integration tests for each subsystem and cross-subsystem interaction.

workers.task_description: Implement Dream Loop for idle-time reflection and continuous self-improvement. When the system is idle (no active tasks in DAG), Dream Loop activates to: (1) Review recent execution history from Blackboard, (2) Apply GRADE framework (Goal-oriented, Reflective, Adaptive, Developmental, Evaluative) to extract actionable insights, (3) Write validated insights to enhanced memory system. Enhance existing memory system (D7) with hierarchical memory layers (short-term working memory, long-term semantic memory, episodic memory). Implement Human Review Gate for heuristic lifecycle management: pending → human review → verified → active. Prevent harmful heuristics from taking effect without human approval (R4). Deliverables include: (1) DreamLoopEngine class with idle-triggered activation, (2) GRADE framework analyzer, (3) InsightWriter for memory persistence, (4) Enhanced memory system with hierarchical layers, (5) HumanReviewGate for heuristic lifecycle (pending→verified→active), (6) integration tests for insight extraction, memory write flow, and human review gate.

workers.task_description: Implement Meta-Loop for self-optimization using single Thompson Sampling (D6) replacing Optuna for parameter tuning, and LLM-as-Optimizer (D5) replacing traditional optimization frameworks. Thompson Sampling maintains posterior distributions over parameter effectiveness, sampling to balance exploration/exploitation. LLM-as-Optimizer analyzes execution metrics (Quality Gate pass rates, token consumption, loop iteration counts) and suggests parameter adjustments. Implement safety constraints: hard upper/lower bounds on all tunable parameters, cooling period between adjustments to prevent oscillation, ±50% amplitude limits per adjustment cycle (R9). Deliverables include: (1) MetaLoopEngine class with Thompson Sampling backend, (2) LLMOptimizer interface for parameter suggestion via structured prompt, (3) ParameterSafetyGuard with hard bounds + cooling period + amplitude limits, (4) execution metrics collector for feedback loop, (5) integration tests for safe parameter adjustment within bounds and Thompson Sampling convergence.

workers.task_description: Implement cross-cutting observability and security infrastructure. (1) Structured logging: JSON-formatted logs with correlation IDs, monotonic timestamps, component tags, and severity levels. (2) Metrics exposure: Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint exposing loop iteration counts, token consumption, Quality Gate pass/reject rates, circuit breaker states, and latency histograms. (3) Distributed tracing: OpenTelemetry-compatible trace spans for cross-component request tracking. (4) guardrails-ai single framework (D8) for input/output validation with configurable guardrail rules. (5) Hash Chain audit log (D9): tamper-evident append-only log where each entry includes SHA-256 hash of previous entry. (6) Multi-layer Prompt Injection detection: input sanitization, Zone 0 hardcoding for critical system prompts, output validation for data exfiltration attempts (R8, RTO < 100ms). (7) RPM rate limit monitoring with exponential backoff (R11). (8) Disk space management with version cleanup strategy and 1GB alert threshold (R12). (9) LLM model version pinning and verification testing (R14). integration_strategy: Blackboard-centric integration with event-driven cross-cutting concerns. CoreInfrastructure establishes the shared Blackboard state mechanism (JSON + atomic rename + per-stage lock). LoopEngine reads from Blackboard to schedule and execute tasks via DAG, writing results back after each stage transition. QualityGate intercepts all Blackboard writes from LoopEngine, validating through three-layer pipeline (Pydantic → LLM Judge → Combined Decision) before commit. SafetyResilience monitors LoopEngine execution via Blackboard state snapshots, activating circuit breakers or fault recovery when anomalies detected. DreamLoop reads Blackboard execution history during idle periods, writing insights back to enhanced memory system via QualityGate validation. MetaLoop reads QualityGate metrics from Blackboard, adjusting LoopEngine parameters within safety bounds. Observability instruments all components via structured logging (correlation IDs), metrics export (Prometheus), and distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry), providing system-wide visibility. All integration occurs through the Blackboard (shared state) and event hooks (cross-cutting concerns like logging, metrics, guardrails), ensuring loose coupling between Workers while maintaining strict data flow integrity.
